title: Java Programming Language
summary: Object-oriented, class-based language designed by James Gosling with the slogan 'Write Once, Run Anywhere' (WORA) using the Java Virtual Machine (JVM).
facts: Originally named 'Oak' after an oak tree outside James Gosling's office.
Officially launched at the SunWorld conference in May 1995.
Popularized Java Applets embedded in web browsers for interactive web graphics.

title: JavaScript (LiveScript)
summary: Dynamic prototype-based scripting language created in 10 days by Brendan Eich for Netscape Navigator 2.0 to add client-side web interactivity.
facts: Originally named Mocha, renamed LiveScript, and quickly renamed JavaScript to leverage Java hype.
Standardized under ECMA International as ECMAScript (ECMA-262) in 1997.
Formed the foundation of dynamic client-side web application programming.

title: Python 1.0 Release
summary: High-level interpreted programming language emphasizing code readability, clean syntax, dynamic typing, and module extensibility.
facts: Created by Guido van Rossum at CWI in the Netherlands, named after Monty Python's Flying Circus.
Version 1.0 released in January 1994 featuring functional programming tools like lambda, map, filter, and reduce.
Gained strong popularity in Unix system administration and scientific scripting.

title: Borland Delphi 1.0
summary: Rapid Application Development (RAD) IDE and Object Pascal compiler for 16-bit Windows, famed for lightning-fast compilation speeds and visual form design.
facts: Chief architect Anders Hejlsberg later went on to design C# at Microsoft.
Visual Component Library (VCL) allowed drag-and-drop database component binding.
Compiled Pascal source code directly into native machine code binaries instantly.

title: PHP / Personal Home Page Tools
summary: Server-side web scripting language created by Rasmus Lerdorf as a set of C binaries to track visits to his online resume.
facts: Originally stood for 'Personal Home Page / Form Interpreter' (PHP/FI).
Rewritten in 1997 by Zeev Suraski and Andi Gutmans to form the core of PHP 3.
Enabled easy HTML page templating and database connectivity for early web servers.
